messages:
maya: quick heads-up — noticed an uptick in Xid/ ECC chatter from eu-west1 last 24h, looks concentrated on a few hosts. not blocking yet but enough to think about spare allocation
aj: can you paste the metric?
maya: sure — aggregated from gpu-health: 
```
metric: gpu.ecc.corrected.count by host
window: 24h
top hosts: host-eu-23 (120), host-eu-67 (98), host-eu-12 (87)
baseline for region: ~12/day per host
```
maya: those three are 7-10x baseline for corrected ECC, plus a handful of Xid 62+ events in the same hosts
sam: any pattern on hardware? same SKU or age?
maya: all A100 80GB v2, purchased 2021-2022, same firmware except host-eu-67 was on an older driver until last week
dara: might be flakey cards starting to degrade — we've seen ECC spikes precede Xid failures before
liam: what does ops-bot say about recent maintenance? ops-bot: automated-notice: "no recent drains or firmware pushes targeted to eu-west1 in past 30 days"
aj: ok. for spare pool sizing we need two numbers: current active GPUs in eu-west1 and observed failure rate (preferably per 1k GPU-months). maya, can you export counts?
maya: eu-west1 active GPUs = 520 (inference pool + training carveouts excluded). looking at last 12 months, we saw 6 complete card replacements and ~40 elevated ECC incidents that required host drains 
aj: that implies roughly 6 failures / 12 months = 1.15% annual hard-fail rate for that region (for our population) — but ECC incident tail suggests more imminent replacements.
sam: for planning I usually use a conservative monthly failure rate p = 0.12% (~1.4% annual) for similar fleets; multiply by N to get expected fails per month. for 520 gpus expected hard failures = 0.624/month
dara: but we should buffer for correlated failures (same batch/firmware) — add a factor of 2x when we see clustering to account for burst mode
liam: so with cluster correlation, worst-case expected = 1.25 GPUs/month. policy question: do we want spare pool to cover 3 months of expected failures (fast replace) or 6 months (supply chain lag)?
aj: cost tradeoff: each hot spare = $X/mo reserved cost + maintenance. current cost per GPU reserved is approx $1,800/mo. holding 5% spares in-region for 520 GPUs = 26 spares ~ $46.8k/mo. that's heavy.
maya: propose hybrid: 3% regional hot spares (~16 GPUs) + cross-region cold pool (on-demand transfer/fast reprovision) sized to cover another 2-3% for surge. that reduces reserved cost while keeping capacity during burst
sam: agree. also add automatic drain-on-first-ecc-threshold and proactive replacement policy for hosts exceeding ECC threshold >50/day for 48h window. that'll reduce emergency replacements and give lead time to draw from pool.
dara: recommend alerting: create a dedicated pager channel for ECC surge with severity when >3 hosts in region exceed threshold simultaneously. also flag firmware-driver mismatches.
liam: can we model spare needs simply: spares_needed = ceil(z * sqrt(N * p * (1-p)) + k * N * p) where z is safety factor (1.96 for 95%) and k accounts for correlation multiplier. example: N=520, p=0.012/month (1.2%), z=1.64 (90%), k=1.5 => spares ≈ ceil(1.64*sqrt(520*0.012*0.988) + 1.5*520*0.012) ≈ ceil(1.64*sqrt(6.17) + 9.36) ≈ ceil(1.64*2.48 + 9.36) ≈ ceil(4.07 + 9.36) = 14
aj: nice, that math gives ~14 which matches the 3% regional hot spare suggestion (15-16). good sanity check.
maya: I'll run a 12-month sim with our actual failure timestamps to estimate burst percentiles and push to the infra playbook
liam: ops ask: if we pull 15 spares, where do they come from? options: 1) reserve new rigs in eu-west1 (costly), 2) maintain a hot-card pool in us-west and enable cross-region routing/fallback, 3) vendor RMA pool with SLA.
sam: option 2 requires network+latency tradeoffs; option 3 needs contract renegotiation. we should do 1 small regional reserve + vendor RMA for replenishment.
dara: action items: maya - run sim and attach 95/99 percentile monthly failure counts; aj - draft cost model for 3% vs 5% regional reserve and cross-region fallback cost; sam - prepare drain/replace playbook and alerting runbook update; liam - check procurement timelines and RMA SLAs.
maya: noted, will share by EOD tomorrow. preliminary table in thread: 
```
scenario A: 3% regional hot spares (16) + vendor RMA 5-day SLA -> estimated monthly cost delta: $29k
scenario B: 5% regional hot spares (26) -> cost delta: $46.8k
scenario C: minimal regional (5) + cross-region pull -> lower cost, higher latency risk
```
aj: thanks. also thumbs on adding driver/firmware mismatch check to onboarding so we avoid accidental regression.
liam: +1. and let's schedule a short oncall drill to exercise cross-region failover next sprint if we go hybrid.
ops-bot: incident-sim: scheduled drill for 2024-10-05 18:00 UTC (reminder will be posted)
maya: thanks team. i'll post the sim and a short recommendation doc in #eng-infra/ops-playbooks when ready. :rocket:
